gloss: to cut off; to clip out; to crop

definitions.gloss: to cut off; to cut out
definitions.explanation: To remove a portion by cutting, such as from paper, fabric, or plants.
To select and extract a portion, especially in photography or video editing.

examples.japanese: {新聞|しんぶん}の{記事|きじ}を{切|き}り{取|と}って{保存|ほぞん}した。
examples.english: I clipped out the newspaper article and saved it.

examples.japanese: {写真|しゃしん}の{不要|ふよう}な{部分|ぶぶん}を{切|き}り{取|と}った。
examples.english: I cropped out the unnecessary parts of the photo.

examples.japanese: {枯|か}れた{枝|えだ}を{切|き}り{取|と}ってください。
examples.english: Please cut off the dead branches.

notes:
{切|き}り{取|と}る is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) formed from {切|き}る (to cut) + {取|と}る (to take). It emphasizes removing a portion by cutting.

ASPECT (ている):
{切|き}り{取|と}っている indicates the cutting action is in progress. {切|き}り{取|と}ってある means something has been cut out and the result remains.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [portion]を{切|き}り{取|と}る — to cut off/out [portion]
- [source]から[portion]を{切|き}り{取|と}る — to cut [portion] from [source]

COMMON PATTERNS:
- クーポンを{切|き}り{取|と}る (cut out a coupon)
- {画像|がぞう}を{切|き}り{取|と}る (crop an image)
- {切|き}り{取|と}り{線|せん} (perforated line, "cut here" line)

MODERN USAGE:
In digital contexts, {切|き}り{取|と}る is the standard term for cropping images or trimming video.
